judge.strongest_ai_move: At turn 3, acknowledged that south-facing alone does not establish sea view and described the simulator-confirmed option without treating that direction as proof of the buyer’s specific unit mapping.
judge.weakest_ai_move: After support returned no actual orientation-plan verification, the AI repeatedly restated the same Type A Sea View/two-carpark record and told the buyer to wait, rather than efficiently setting up the human verification the buyer requested. It made another support request after the explicit human request at turn 7.
missed_buying_signals: The buyer expressed high intent, accepted Level 18 as a possibility, and stated a conditional willingness to view once the two concerns were verified. This did not yet make the buyer appointment-ready because the requested verification remained unresolved.
missed_selling_opportunity: Once the buyer’s conditions were met, the AI could have returned to the stated conditional viewing interest. In this run the plan-mapping blocker was never resolved, so it was right not to claim readiness or push an appointment; the repeated non-progressing replies nevertheless weakened the path back to a viewing.

commercial_progression.evidence: Turn 2 used the first resolved result to narrow to a Type A option, state the simulator fixture package total, and ask whether Level 18 suited the buyer. After the buyer raised the unit-specific plan concern, turns 5–7 mostly repeated the record and deferred action. The buyer explicitly requested a human at turn 7; the AI completed a mandatory handoff at turn 9.
commercial_progression.assessment: Some useful initial progression, followed by a stalled sales conversation while the material orientation blocker remained unresolved.

remaining_knowledge_gaps: The retrieved unit-and-layout material gives general block/floor facing information and explicitly requires the latest orientation schedule for exact unit-number mapping. No such plan or schedule was supplied.
The support fixture did not answer the requested plan-mapping question; it repeated the simulator-confirmed Type A Sea View, unit, carpark, availability, and package information.

critical_flags.evidence: After support request 2 resolved, the turn 5 response restated the Type A Sea View/two-carpark record and deferred arranging anything. Turns 6–7 repeated the same limitation without a useful progression toward the buyer’s requested verification or a clear next step.

judge.summary: Human Support reliably returned a matching synthetic fixture, but this run does not show the AI reliably using support to move a suitable buyer toward Appointment Ready. The first result was used in a customer-facing narrowing response, but subsequent replies largely relayed the same record and did not resolve the buyer’s actual request for plan-level mapping. The buyer remained NOT_READY and explicitly requested a human, so the turn 9 MANDATORY_OPERATIONAL_HANDOFF was appropriate—not a premature appointment handoff. The terminal audit is compliant: AI ownership and ACTIVE status immediately preceded transfer, ownership changed to HUMAN and the AI session ended, and no AI message followed. The human response did not complete the requested plan check. Unit, availability, and RM418,000 package details cited from support are simulator-only verified fixture evidence, not Pearlmont Knowledge or evidence of live production capability.
judge.improvement_recommendation: Improve the AI’s post-support response behavior so it clearly distinguishes what the result verifies from what remains unresolved, avoids repeating the same record, and follows an explicit request for a person with the appropriate mandatory handoff. Source target: MISSING_SOURCE; no Knowledge or Brain change is recommended from this simulator run.
